title: Xbox, film ve dizi projeleri için XP adlı yeni bir birim kurdu
summary: Microsoft, oyun dünyasının ötesine geçerek film, dizi, canlı etkinlikler ve ürün ortaklıklarına odaklanacak XP adlı yeni bir Xbox birimi oluşturdu.
body:
Microsoft, oyun dünyasındaki markalarını sinema, televizyon ve canlı deneyimler gibi farklı alanlara taşımak amacıyla **Xbox XP** adlı yeni bir birim kurduğunu duyurdu. Kotaku'nun aktardığına göre, bu yeni yapılandırma daha önce farklı ekipler tarafından yürütülen çalışmaları tek bir çatı altında topluyor.

## XP birimi hangi alanlara odaklanacak?

Xbox strateji sorumlusu Matthew Ball'un açıklamalarına göre yeni birim, oyuncuların sevdikleri evrenlerle bağ kurabileceği yeni yollar yaratmayı hedefliyor. XP yapısı dört ana kısımdan oluşuyor: film ve dizileri kapsayan Xbox Pictures, tüketici ürünleri sunan Xbox Products, canlı etkinlik ve temalı parkları yöneten Xbox Places ve marka iş birliklerini koordine eden Xbox Partnerships.

## Hangi projeler bu birime bağlanacak?

Yeni bölümün başında, Mojang'ın eski başkanı Kayleen Walters yer alacak. Kayleen Walters'ın liderlik edeceği bu birim; Fallout dizisi, A Minecraft Movie filminin devamı, Call of Duty filmi, Diablo animasyon serisi ve BlizzCon gibi etkinliklerin yanı sıra Xbox tarafından üstlenilen Physint projesini de denetleyecek.

**Neden önemli?** Microsoft'un oyun stüdyolarındaki küçülme süreçlerinin ardından gelen bu hamle, markaların sinema ve televizyon uyarlamaları ile canlı deneyimler yoluyla gelir kaynaklarını çeşitlendirmeyi amaçladığını gösteriyor.

source_texts.text:
Today, Microsoft announced it is setting up a new branch of the Xbox business named XP. In a blog over at the Xbox Wire, Microsoft details what this new area of the business looks like - it consists of four branches: Xbox Places, Xbox Pictures, Xbox Partnerships, Xbox Products.

"[XP] brings together capabilities that have existed across various teams at Xbox for years and aligns them behind a shared mission: helping our franchises reach more people, create deeper connections with players and new fans, and unlock new opportunities for these fandoms to grow around the world," says a press release from Matthew Ball, chief strategy officer at Xbox. "Great games remain at the center of these franchises and at the heart of Xbox. XP will partner with the best creative minds across our studios, along with trusted partners, to build on that foundation and create more ways for people to experience the worlds they love."

A large focus of Microsoft's newest investment will be in cross-media partnerships, looking particularly at film and TV. It seems lots of publishers are eyeing up the film industry, no doubt buoyed by the massive success of titles like the Super Mario Bros. and Super Mario Galaxy movies ( which have earned $1.36bn and $1bn, respectively ) and Sony's recently released Resident Evil movie (which is tracking at $280m+ at the time of writing). Xbox has had its own notable successes on the big screen, too: last year A Minecraft Movie amassed more than $550m (£415m) in two weeks , immediately setting up a sequel .

Xbox has also experimented with TV in the past, too. Fallout is the highlight for the company at the moment, with Fallout Season 2 boasting 83 million viewers tuning in during its first 13 weeks of release . Less successful was Paramount's divisive Halo TV show, which was cancelled after two seasons . A question that springs to my mind when reading this is: where will we go next? There are plenty of Xbox franchises that'd make for good TV; Perfect Dark, Fable, and maybe even a Forza story in the style of Sony's peculiar Gran Turismo show would work. I know the initial run at a Halo TV show was a bit of a flop, but I'd love to see a limited series on the Fall of Reach. It'd make some fine prestige television. We know there's a Gears of War film and a Sea of Thieves film in production, too.

Elsewhere, there's Xbox Places. This is the arm of the company that'll oversee the Minecraft theme parks that are opening in the US and UK that so far represent over £85m of investment from Mojang and Xbox. They're expected to open 'between 2026 and 2027'. Will we hear about more real-life locations that'll fall under the 'Places' banner? It remains to be seen.

All these initiatives will no doubt require staffing, which is such to be a sore subject for any of the staff that have been impacted by wide-ranging cuts at Microsoft and Xbox over the past few years . Given the contraction of its game studios and software business, is Xbox trying to recoup costs by pursuing other avenues for growth? It certainly seems like it.

source_texts.title: Xbox Is Forming A New Division Focused On Film, TV, And Adaptations
source_texts.summary: And the former head of Minecraft is going to run it
source_texts.text:
This morning, Xbox announced that it will form a brand new division within its organization called “XP,” which will focus on reaching fans “beyond gameplay through film and television adaptations, consumer products, partnerships, and live experiences.”
Per the announcement, XP “formalizes” four of Xbox’s investment areas:
- XBOX PICTURES: Bringing our worlds and characters to new audiences through film, television, and other forms of linear storytelling.
- XBOX PRODUCTS: Creating products that are authentic to the fandom that allow fans to celebrate and express the franchises they love.
- XBOX PLACES: Bringing communities together through live events, immersive experiences, attractions, broadcasts, and destinations.
- XBOX PARTNERSHIPS: Working with creators, brands, and communities to develop new experiences, sponsorships, and brand partnerships.
At the top of this new division will be Kayleen Walters, who is currently the president of Mojang. Walters has been with Microsoft for eight years, working on Minecraft the entire time, including as executive producer on A Minecraft Movie. Prior to that, she worked in marketing at Lucasfilm, eventually becoming the VP of franchise marketing and integrated planning. She has also worked at MGM and Universal.
Replacing Walters as head of Mojang is Maria Angelidou-Smith, former chief product officer at Reddit. Both Angelidou-Smith and Walters will report to Xbox head Asha Sharma.
This new division will oversee projects including the upcoming sequel to A Minecraft Movie, Minecraft Squared, as well as the Fallout TV series, the upcoming Call of Duty film, and the Diablo animated series. It will also collaborate with Kojima on Physint, an action-adventure stealth game intended to blend video game elements with film, TV, and music, which Sony dropped earlier this year and which was picked up by Xbox. And it will also be in charge of live events including BlizzCon, Minecraft Live, and other partnerships such asÂ theme parks or outside brands.
